expectation: This should represent the difference in lunar pull that drives tides.

effect: The Moon’s differential pull is now represented; the next step is to apply it to the sea.

reason: The uneven pull should affect the sea and begin the tidal motion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Tracing the tide from the Moon’s uneven pull to its local response was worthwhile: it showed how coastal geography shapes tides rather than lunar distance alone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to combine the exposed beach with the hollows was a frustrating dead end; the beach had no available combinations.

surprise.text: I expected the exposed beach to lead to the pools, but the hollows first needed to be filled by the coastal tide.

arbitrary.text: Using Earth’s rotation to advance the falling tide felt somewhat abstract, even though it produced the expected result both times.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more natural processes, especially if they connect physical mechanisms to a visible landscape as the tidal sequence did.
